clue.text: Pause for inspiration

parts.note: inspiration is read literally as drawing in air, so a pause in which to take a breath becomes a respite or short rest

explanation.surface: A writer stops and waits for an idea to come.
explanation.definitionFit: A short interval of rest or relief from pressure is a gap in which one can recover one's wind.

clue.text: Will mesmerise during tenth rally

indicators.note: the answer sits within the run of letters across the words tenth rally, lasting during them

explanation.surface: A tenth rally of some movement will hypnotise the crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: To captivate or spellbind someone is to hold their attention completely, as a hypnotist does.

clue.text: Seaweed that's brown and green initially

parts.note: tan is a light brown colour

indicators.note: initially asks for the opening letter of the word green

explanation.surface: Some seaweed is coloured brown with a green start.
explanation.definitionFit: Tang is a name for large coarse brown seaweeds such as wrack or kelp.

clue.text: I do, with the Parisienne, make an attempt at excessive love

parts.note: taken as written
la is the feminine form of 'the' in French, as a Parisian woman would use it
an attempt is a try

explanation.surface: A bride says her vows, trying hard at a love that goes too far.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I do' suggests a wedding vow but simply supplies its own letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Worship of an idol extends figuratively to extreme admiration or devotion for any person or thing.

clue.text: Voracious newsman in grey

indicators.note: in places the newsman inside the colour word

parts.note: taken as written
ED is short for editor, the chief newsman

explanation.surface: A ravenous journalist dressed in grey.
explanation.definitionFit: A voracious person has an insatiable appetite, wanting more food than is needed.

clue.text: Notes received by press on payday?

definitions.text: Notes received by press on payday?

parts.words: Notes received by press on payday?
parts.note: the press is read as a newspaper, whose wages would be cash of a papery kind, i.e. banknotes

explanation.surface: Journalists collect their pay packets at the end of the month.
explanation.definitionFit: Banknotes are currency printed on paper rather than minted coins.

clue.text: Picture decapitated parrot behind bars

indicators.note: being behind bars means being enclosed, so the bird's remainder goes inside

parts.note: a cage is made of bars

indicators.note: decapitated removes the head, the first letter of the parrot's name

parts.note: Poll, or Polly, is a traditional name for a parrot

explanation.surface: An image of a beheaded parrot locked in a cage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'decapitated' turns POLL into OLL, which goes inside CAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A collage is an artwork made by sticking assorted materials onto a backing, a kind of picture.

clue.text: One in France has the full amount with part being detrimental to health

parts.note: un is French for one
the whole is the full amount
some means a part or portion

explanation.surface: A Frenchman claims all of something, part of which is bad for you.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that harms bodily or moral wellbeing is unhealthy or harmful.

clue.text: Phaeton's parts used to make another carriage

indicators.note: the letters are broken into parts and reassembled to build a different word

explanation.surface: Bits of one horse-drawn coach are reused to build another.
explanation.walkthrough: Here the possessive S of 'Phaeton's' is counted as a letter of the fodder; a phaeton is itself a light carriage, hence 'another'.
explanation.definitionFit: A stanhope is a light open one-seated horse-drawn vehicle, named after a nineteenth-century clergyman.

clue.text: Join the bandwagon, say, of power supporter

indicators.note: say signals that the phrase is spoken and its sound gives the answer

parts.note: to pile on is to join in with what everyone else is doing

explanation.surface: Someone joins a popular cause and supports a powerful figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Pylons are steel towers holding up overhead electricity cables.

clue.text: Huge brute in the east

parts.note: an elephant is a large beast or brute
taken as written
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A large animal found in the East.
explanation.definitionFit: Something immense or ponderous is as big as one of the largest land animals.

clue.text: One not telling the truth heard on this instrument

indicators.note: heard means the phrase is listened to and its sound gives the answer

parts.note: a person telling untruths is a liar

explanation.surface: A fibber is heard performing on a musical instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A lyre is a small harp used in ancient Greece.

clue.text: Stupid talk about a less hairy rush

parts.note: a balder person has less hair
to dash is to rush

explanation.surface: Nonsense spoken about a balding man in a hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is a link here, not a reversal or container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Balderdash is senseless chatter or nonsense.

clue.text: Soothing words over yonder

definitions.meaning: a comforting phrase said to calm someone upset
pointing to a place at a distance, said twice for emphasis

explanation.definitionFit: The doubled word is both an expression of comfort and a repeated indication of location in that place.

clue.text: Cut back on firm fish

indicators.note: back means the word for cut is read in reverse order

parts.note: to clip is to cut
hard means firm

explanation.surface: A fishmonger is forced to cut back on a firm.
explanation.definitionFit: The pilchard is a small oily fish of the herring family, also called a sardine.

clue.text: Make learners we included prosper

parts.note: to do can mean to make
taken as written
L is the learner-driver plate letter, so two learners give LL

explanation.surface: Teaching students alongside ourselves helps them succeed.
explanation.definitionFit: To flourish or succeed is to thrive.

clue.text: Slovenly woman might start Len off

indicators.note: off suggests the letters are thrown out of order and rearranged

explanation.surface: An untidy woman might set Len going.
explanation.definitionFit: A slattern is an old term for a dirty, untidy woman.

clue.text: Jack's posh way is clearly wrong

parts.note: a jack is a sailor, AB for able seaman, with the 's adding an S
U stands for upper-class usage
RD is short for road, a way

explanation.surface: A sailor's affected manner is obviously mistaken.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ridiculous or illogical is plainly unreasonable.

clue.text: Dutch philosopher carries little weight in Spain perhaps

indicators.note: carries means the rearranged country holds the small weight within it
perhaps hints the country name may be arranged differently

parts.note: oz, an ounce, is a small unit of weight

explanation.surface: A thinker from the Netherlands is lightweight in Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' turns SPAIN into SPINA, and 'carries' puts OZ inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Baruch Spinoza was a seventeenth-century rationalist thinker from Amsterdam.

clue.text: Stupid, unlike crossword solvers

definitions.meaning: solvers always have hints to work from, so being without them is the opposite

explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means both ignorant and literally lacking hints, which solvers never lack.

clue.text: Building on a site in Eastern Europe

indicators.note: building suggests the letters are put together in a new construction

explanation.surface: Construction work on a plot in the east of Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link: the answer is one country of Eastern Europe, a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Estonia is a Baltic state, one of the countries forming the eastern part of the continent.

clue.text: Celestial being's turn of phrase

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: a turn of the word suggests its letters twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: An angel's way with words.
explanation.definitionFit: A seraph is an angel of the highest order in the heavenly hierarchy.

clue.text: I last but seven to score

definitions.text: I last but seven to score

parts.words: I last but seven to score
parts.note: a score is twenty, so counting back seven places from the end of twenty gives the position the speaker holds

explanation.surface: A player says they finished just behind in a scoring contest.
explanation.definitionFit: In a sequence of twenty, the item seven places before the end stands at ordinal position number thirteen.

clue.text: Staunch supporter

definitions.meaning: to stop a flow, as of blood
the stalk that holds up a flower or leaf

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for checking a flow and a noun for a plant stalk bearing a bloom.

clue.text: A Frenchman so upset by the prophet

parts.note: M is short for Monsieur, a Frenchman's title

indicators.note: upset in a down clue turns the little word upside down, reading it backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A Frenchman is so distressed by the Old Testament seer.
explanation.definitionFit: Amos is a Hebrew prophet whose book is in the Old Testament.

clue.text: She wept as I love Ben going round the outside

indicators.note: the outside means the cycled name wraps around the other letters
going round moves the last letter of the name to the front, cycling it

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A woman cried because her love Ben went off outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going round' turns BEN into NBE, and IO sits between its N and BE.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Niobe's children were slain and she was turned into a stone that ever weeps.

clue.text: Fellows with model beat a retreat first it was their assistance in the crime

indicators.note: to retreat is to fall back, here suggesting the letters move back into a new order

parts.note: men are fellows
the Model T was an early Ford car, giving T

explanation.surface: Men help each other flee from the scene of a crime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' puts ABET, from shuffling BEAT, before MEN and T; the wording around it is a loose link.
explanation.definitionFit: Aiding someone to commit an offence is legally called abetting, the help of an accomplice.

clue.text: Make little effort to enjoy oneself?

definitions.meaning: to avoid hard work or exertion
to relax and have a pleasant time

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both slacking off and relaxing comfortably.
